terms.meaning: The agent that checks the full set of records for shared work, calibration and sequencing problems.
An extra adjustment that changes a score for reporting, while the original score stays unchanged.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Why the reduce step is separate
sections.what: The docstring explains that portfolio-level properties need every record at once, and that the portfolio type cannot be built without the reconciler.
sections.why: Running the reconciler per process would compare a process with itself and always pass.
sections.watch_out: Any new path that builds a portfolio must go through the reconciler.

sections.name: UnschedulablePortfolio
sections.title: Cycle error
sections.what: Defines the error raised when the prerequisite map loops back on itself, and lists the loops in the message.
sections.why: A plan built from a loop would be arbitrary, and it would look like a valid plan.
sections.watch_out: The message asks for the dependency to be fixed in the source record, not for the sequence to be changed.

sections.name: Portfolio (part 1)
sections.title: Portfolio object and checks
sections.what: Holds the records and the reconciliation result, and checks the record count and the adjustment names when built.
sections.why: The reconciliation field has no default, so a portfolio cannot exist without it. The checks stop the portfolio from being built with too few records or with broken adjustments.
sections.watch_out: The raw records are kept beside the adjustments, so reports must not treat the raw scores as final.

sections.name: Portfolio: calibrated_score
sections.title: Calibrated score lookup
sections.what: Returns the adjusted score for a process and dimension if one exists, and the raw score otherwise. An unknown dimension raises an error.
sections.why: Every report needs the same rule for reading scores, so the rule lives in one place.
sections.watch_out: The code notes that at most one adjustment can exist per process and dimension, which keeps the result the same regardless of order.

sections.name: reconcile_portfolio
sections.title: Reconcile function
sections.what: Sends all records to the reconciler, raises an error if cycles are found and not allowed, and returns the portfolio.
sections.why: This is the only place a portfolio is produced. Running it once means the checks see the full set.
sections.watch_out: It needs at least two records, so a single-process run cannot reach this step.

summary: Runs the reconciler once over all finished records to produce a portfolio, and refuses to build a portfolio without that reconciliation.
purpose: Make sure the portfolio-wide checks, such as shared enablers, calibration and sequencing, always run on the full set.
why: A portfolio-level property cannot be checked for one process alone. The required reconciliation field makes it impossible to build a portfolio without running the reconciler.
how: reconcile_portfolio sends all records to the reconciler. If the prerequisite graph has a cycle and cycles are not allowed, it raises an error. Otherwise it builds the Portfolio. The Portfolio checks that it has enough records and that every adjustment names a process in the set. calibrated_score returns the adjusted value when one exists, otherwise the raw score.
inputs: A model client, a run context, a list of finished process records, and an option to allow cycles.
outputs: A Portfolio object holding the records and the reconciliation result, or an error.
risks: Setting allow_cycles to true lets an arbitrary plan through, and nothing downstream will detect that. Raw scores are kept unchanged, so reports must read calibrated values through calibrated_score.
debug: A cycle error lists the processes in the loop. A too-small portfolio error gives the count. A dangling adjustment error lists the missing ids. For wrong scores, check the adjustment list for that process and dimension.
